subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and volume qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and volume qualification

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the team this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a clean proposal: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: real-time customer support augmentation (chat + short text completions) + nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Expected traffic pattern: steady baseline with 1–2 short bursts during product launches. You mentioned spikes around new feature rollouts.

Questions we had to qualify cost/overage:
1) Estimated monthly token volume (input + output): can you confirm rough monthly tokens and top-of-peak concurrent requests?
2) Typical tokens per request (avg and 95th pct): this helps pick batching/latency profiles.
3) Target economics: you said target budget in the ballpark of $X/1M tokens — can you confirm a target $/1M tokens (range is fine)?
4) Burst behavior: how long are bursts (seconds/minutes) and how big (requests/s)?

What we can offer / next steps:
- I attached our rate limits & overage reference (redwood-rate-limits.pdf) and a quick cost worksheet. High level: hosted API has flexible quotas and predictable per-token pricing; we support short-term quota increases for bursts and pre-purchased burst buffers to avoid throttles.
- If you expect sustained high throughput, Dedicated reserved capacity gives better unit economics and guaranteed throughput.

Could you reply with the approximate monthly token estimate, avg tokens per request, and expected burst size/duration? Also, loop in your procurement contact when you’re ready and I’ll send a formal estimate.

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up tomorrow to review numbers and share an initial quote. 

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.c@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-rate-limits.pdf
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and volume qualification

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Answers inline below.

Monthly token estimate: ~200M tokens/month (input+output). This is current expected consumption for Phase 1. If all goes well, Phase 2 could be 600–800M.
Tokens per request: average ~300 tokens (chat + metadata). 95th percentile ~900 tokens.
Burst behavior: launches produce bursts of ~400–600 requests/s lasting 3–8 minutes. Baseline traffic is ~20–30 req/s.
Target economics: we’re aiming for ~ $20 / 1M tokens as a target price (negotiable based on commit).

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood support burst windows of that size without throttling? If we exceed quota, what are typical overage rates and billing terms?
- For hosted API, how quickly can we get a temporary quota increase for a scheduled rollout?

Procurement contact (looping in): procurement@acme.io — they’ll handle the SOW/PO.

Appreciate a quick sketch of options (hosted with burst buffer vs dedicated reserved) and a ballpark monthly cost at the $20/1M target for 200M tokens.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Acme Inc.
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme pricing sketch (200M, burst requirements)

Marissa / Rishi — notes from Alex’s reply and suggested approach: 

Client asks: 200M tokens/month, avg 300 tokens, bursts 400–600 req/s for ~5 mins, target $20/1M.

Quick pricing sketch (ballpark):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): list $/1M = $35 — to hit $20/1M we’d need a committed discount. For 200M tokens at $20/1M = $4,000/month. With hosted and burst buffer (prepaid 50% buffer), we can keep throttles off for scheduled launches.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): effective unit economics can drop to ~$12–$15/1M depending on committed monthly GPU hours; requires commitment and lead time for capacity. For 200M tokens estimated cost ~ $2,600–$3,000/month.

Overage/rate-limits policy we should propose: 
- Scheduled burst increases: we can provision a temporary quota increase within 24 hours for hosted customers (same-day for most requests if capacity available).
- Prepaid burst buffer: pre-pay X tokens that apply before overage billing — recommended for launch windows.
- Overage terms: overage billed monthly at a higher tiered rate (e.g., +25% above committed unit price) unless a one-time buffer is used. We can be more flexible in the commercial (cap on first-month overage or credit).

Suggested next steps for the quote: 
1) Send Alex two priced options in writing: Hosted with 50% prepaid burst buffer (including how quota increases are handled) and Dedicated reserved price for 12-month commit.
2) Include a one-time launch buffer credit (cover first burst overage up to X tokens) to remove friction.
3) Provide sample SLA around throttling behavior and lead time for quota increases.

I’ll draft the estimate. Marissa: want me to include the Dedicated vs Hosted TCO table and the overage cap language?

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.io>, Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and volume qualification

Alex — thanks for the detailed numbers, that helps a lot. Attaching a quick estimate (acme-overage-estimate.xlsx) and our rate limits doc for reference. High-level answers: 

1) Burst support: yes — hosted API supports short bursts at the sizes you described by combining temporary quota increases + a prepaid burst buffer to avoid throttling. For unscheduled spikes we have tiered overage protection, but we recommend scheduling launches where possible so we can guarantee capacity.

2) Quota increases: typical turnaround is 24 hours for requested increases. For scheduled rollouts we can often do same-day provisioning if requested morning-of and capacity is available. For guaranteed capacity we recommend Dedicated.

3) Overage terms: proposed commercial approach:
- Prepaid burst buffer (recommended): one-time prepaid tokens applied during bursts, not billed as overage.
- If prepaid buffer exhausted: overage billed at committed unit price + 25% (we can cap the first month’s overage to avoid sticker shock).
- We’re open to a short-term credit on the first launch (e.g., cover up to 5M tokens of overage) to get you comfortable.

Ballpark monthly numbers at $20/1M target: 
- Hosted w/ 50% prepaid buffer (200M): ~$4,000/month + buffer prepay (~$2,000 one-time).
- Dedicated (12-month commit): ~$2,700/month (requires sizing call for exact GPU profile).

Next steps: I’ll send a formal two-option quote by EOD tomorrow and propose a 30-min follow-up to review. Marissa: would you like to proceed with the quote including the 5M overage credit?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.c@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme-overage-estimate.xlsx, redwood-rate-limits.pdf
